duplicate_verdict.formal_duplicate: No evidence. Coverage state is "Crawled - currently not indexed", not "Duplicate, Google chose different canonical", and googleCanonical is empty, so Google has not named another URL as the canonical.
duplicate_verdict.practical_verdict: Probable cluster-level redundancy / low-value filter, not a copy. Body text is not duplicated (max 5-gram overlap 2.8%, TF-IDF cosine 0.47), but the guide is a hub that restates, in H2 form, topics that seven named sibling pages own: 20% credit (section-24-tax-credit-20-percent-basic-rate-relief), what is s24 (section-24-mortgage-interest-restriction-uk-landlords), arrangement fees (mortgage-arrangement-fees-deductible-landlord), SA105 (section-24-self-assessment-tax-return), worked example and cap (how-to-calculate-section-24-tax-credit-step-by-step), commercial (section-24-commercial-property-complete-guide), April 2027 reducer (2027-property-tax-rates-section-24-relief-uk-landlords). 11 of 16 cluster URLs inspected today are crawled-not-indexed, so the pattern is the cluster, not this URL alone.
duplicate_verdict.stale_signal: Most of the CNI cluster was last crawled 2026-05-15 to 2026-07-19; the 2026-10-09 rewrite has not been recrawled. The verdict is on the May version.
duplicate_verdict.how_it_differs: Only this page frames the topic in HMRC's own term, "residential finance costs" (SA105 box 44/45 wording, PIM2054), and answers the "which costs count" question as one list: interest, arrangement and broker fees, overdraft, refinancing, loan to buy furniture, alternative finance, plus exclusions. Bing proves that angle: 37 top-3 queries, 117 clicks, mostly residential finance costs / relief for finance costs / HMRC wording. No sibling targets that phrase in title or H1.
duplicate_verdict.how_it_could_differ: Own the finance-cost definition (what is and is not a residential finance cost, with box 44/45 and the cap) and hand the credit mechanics, arrangement-fee detail, worked example and 2027 reducer to the sibling pages by link instead of restating them. Link in body to those siblings and to /section-24 (it links to none of them today), and get it linked from the pillar and the indexed siblings. Add the unanswered Bing queries (27) as FAQ or H3.

into_non_body.anchor: Finance Costs Under Section 24: What Counts and What You Can ClaimSection 24 does not stop residential landlords claiming finance costs. It changes how the relief is given: instead of deducting mortgage interest and other dwelling-related loan costs from rental profit, you get a basic-rate tax reducer worth 20% of those costs for 2026/27 (rising to 22% from 2027/28). This guide sets out exactly which costs qualify as residential finance costs, which fall outside the restriction, how the three-part cap works, where the figures go on the SA105 self-assessment pages, and a full worked example.9 min read10 April 2026
